items.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021
items.q: she was the only woman in the band with all these men... everybody had mutual respect for her.

ctx.x: that. And if they wanted to do anything we’d have to do it ourself. And that was the thing. You come here, you have to take care of your business, you have to learn and you have to have some discipline, and we’d do what we need to do ourself. If a window’s broken you have to go do your part and fix the window. If the door was broken or you need some carpentry work or some ceiling work you’d do it. So it was like a self storage you know, that anything you want done — so he wanted a sink I think, in the room, so…
Did it change the dynamic of the band when June Tyson became part of the group? And do you think it was difficult for her being the only woman in the group?

No because she was the kind of woman that could be with me and it wasn’t about those sexy things and all that B.S. you know. It was nothing. Because she carried herself in that manner that you know she was more like in the family, like a sister you know. And that’s the way she carried herself. So she was the only woman in the band with all these men, you know, but everybody had mutual respect for her.
